overview.summary: Locksmiths install, repair and maintain locks and security systems, and help people who are locked out, always checking first that they have the right to enter.
overview.problems: They keep homes, businesses and vehicles secure and help people get back in safely and legally.
overview.worksWith: Home and business owners, property managers, landlords, builders and sometimes police or insurers.
overview.workplaces: Workshops, shops, vehicles and customers' premises, and many locksmiths are self-employed.

timeline.title: Plan jobs and load the van
timeline.description: The locksmith checks bookings, parts and tools.
timeline.why: The right parts save return trips.

timeline.title: Fitting and upgrading locks
timeline.description: The locksmith installs new locks and strengthens doors for customers who want better security.

timeline.title: Cutting keys and repairs
timeline.description: The locksmith cuts keys and repairs or replaces worn locks.
timeline.why: Keys and locks wear out and need care.

timeline.title: Lockout calls
timeline.description: The locksmith verifies the customer's identity and right to enter before helping.
timeline.why: Helping the wrong person could enable a break-in.

timeline.title: Advising customers
timeline.description: The locksmith suggests sensible security upgrades for the property.

timeline.title: Emergency call-outs
timeline.description: People get locked out or doors are damaged at any hour.

responsibilities: Helping people who are locked out after checking they are entitled to enter
Following the law and professional codes
challenges: Emergency call-outs happen at night and at weekends.
Customers can be stressed or locked out in bad weather.
Strict legal and ethical duties apply, including checking identity.
Self-employed locksmiths must find customers and manage money.
Scams in the industry make customer trust important.
Training, background checks or licensing are required in many places.
workEnvironment: Mobile work at customers' homes, businesses and vehicles, plus a workshop for key cutting and repairs. Hours often include emergency call-outs. Many locksmiths run their own small business.
rewards: The option to run your own business
tradeoffs: Earnings that vary by country and area

activity.title: Learn how a lock works and explain it
steps: Read how a basic pin-tumbler lock and key work from a trusted educational source.
Draw a diagram showing the key, the pins and the cylinder.
Build a simple model from cardboard and straws to show how the right key lines up the pins.
Explain it to a family member.
Note whether understanding mechanisms felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise understanding a mechanism and explaining it clearly.
activity.safety: Do not try to open, pick or tamper with any lock that is not yours, and ask an adult before taking anything apart. Opening locks without permission is illegal.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
